quiz.where: Final test, test spot-cleared-early, option c "The grilling session was too short to be useful." (line 407) and option a "`/to-spec` ran too late; it belonged before the grilling." (line 403)
quiz.problem: Weak distractors. The prompt's own facts rule out two of the three: it says the spec "misses half her decisions", so the decisions existed (which rules out c), and a spec written before any grilling would have had none of them (which rules out a). The question then comes down to b against d, and d points at nothing the prompt mentions. Option c's feedback also claims something the Lesson never supports ("Forty-five minutes is plenty."), even though the prompt calls it a big feature and line 61 says there is no limit.
quiz.evidence: Prompt at line 402: "Priya grilled a big feature for 45 minutes, typed `/clear` to free up space ... misses half her decisions." Line 61: "a plan can need as few as three questions or as many as fifty ... There's no limit". Line 408: "Forty-five minutes is plenty." Line 186 teaches that a filling window makes the model reason less sharply, and Priya cleared "to free up space". 'Too much to fit' is therefore the tempting misconception. It stays wrong because /clear had emptied the window before /to-spec ran (to-spec/SKILL.md:7 works from the current conversation).
quiz.fix: Reword option c only (position, order and [x] unchanged; the right option b stays shorter): "- [ ] Forty-five minutes of answers was too much for `/to-spec` to fit in one spec." with feedback "  > Length wasn't the problem: `/clear` had already emptied the conversation, so none of those answers reached `/to-spec`."
